I really want to emphasize how disgustingly third world this is.

Retards on mopeds blocking traffic so they can make pennies on food app delivery is an ever-present reality in Mexico, El Salvador, the Philippines, insert turd world shithole here. I have no idea how they make a profit in those countries particularly when you consider that gas is usually more expensive in these places than it is in the U.S. (To give an example, gas in central New Jersey is about $2.89/gallon right now, while gas in Guadalajara---where I lived up until a few months ago---is MXN $20.96/liter, or $4.30/gallon. Reminder that Mexico is an oil-producing state and a member of OPEC.)

The general atmosphere of cars and bikes zig-zagging everywhere, clogged streets due to nobody understanding that the left lane is for passing only, pricks blasting their motorcycles at 11pm because they think mufflers are for homos, all of this is third world and it's why living there gradually becomes unpleasant to the point of driving you insane. The day I arrived in the Philippines, I got stressed out on the taxi ride to my apartment because of the sheer number of people on the road, jeepneys that explode randomly and kill their passengers, dickheads on mopeds weaving between cars during standstill traffic, hustlers running up to the car trying to sell you 7Eleven shit at a markup.

All of this is now present everywhere in the U.S. to some degree, except MAYBE some rural towns. There are bums begging with signs in the strip malls outside of Poughkeepsie. There are loiterers napping in the cafe at the Middletown QuickChek. There's some guy of indeterminate ethnicity, an unkempt beard, and the stink of urine patrolling the Panera Bread entrance in the middle of New Jersey suburbia giving everyone who walks in the evil eye. And you have libtards pretending this is Normal and Good because they would rather the bearded schizo gut them like a fish then admit the "chuds" are right.

We don't have to live like this, and we won't. We will purge the subway until it's as clean and quiet as the trains in Tokyo. We will make smoking marijuana in public punishable with public canings. And we will impound every illegal DoorDash moped and crush it in a compacter.

LOOK: Special Assistant to the President Antonio Lagdameo Jr. and DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian distribute additional relief goods in Capiz province on Thursday, October 23.

They assured that the Marcos administration is extending aid to the victims of the massive flooding that occurred on October 18–19.

They were joined by former Senator Mar Roxas, Special Assistant to the President Lorenzo Sagucio Jr., Capiz 1st District Rep. Howard Guintu, Vice Gov. Jaime Magbanua, Roxas City Mayor Ronnie Dadivas, and Panay Mayor Sonny Besa.

📷 DSWD Western Visayas and Office of Mayor Dadivas | via Tara Yap
